In this work, we propose a method to automatically annotate the document layout of over 1 million PubMed Central™ PDF articles and generate a high-quality document layout dataset called PubLayNet. The dataset contains over 360k page samples and covers typical document layout elements such as text, title, list, figure, and table.

The annotation quality of a PDF page is defined as the ratio of the area of textboxes, images, and geometric shapes that are annotated to the area of textboxes, images, and geometric shapes within the main text box of the page. Non-title pages of which the annotation quality is less than 99% are excluded from PubLayNet, which is an extremely high standard to control the noise in PubLayNet at a low level.
